rhymes.title: Reagan and Gorbachev meet in Geneva
rhymes.rhyme: The first US-Soviet leaders' summit in six years, held while arms talks were stalled. This week's Shenzhen meeting is the first ever of US, Chinese and Russian leaders together.

rhymes.title: Cairo Conference: Roosevelt, Churchill, Chiang Kai-shek
rhymes.rhyme: The US and Chinese leaders met in person, days before the US and Soviet leaders met at Tehran. The three never sat together, which is why a US-China-Russia trilateral has no precedent.

rhymes.title: Tehran Conference: Roosevelt, Churchill, Stalin
rhymes.rhyme: Great-power leaders met in Iran to bargain over spheres and timing; Iran was the venue then and is the battlefield now.

rhymes.title: US Embassy in Tehran seized; 444-day hostage crisis begins
rhymes.rhyme: The start of the US-Iran rupture that frames today's conflict; crises with Iran have run long once they start.

rhymes.title: Anglo-French landings at Suez; ceasefire under US pressure
rhymes.rhyme: A chokepoint closed by war and reopened only after diplomacy (the canal stayed blocked into 1957): physical reopening lags the ceasefire.

rhymes.title: Arab oil embargo
rhymes.rhyme: An oil supply shock that ran through the November of its year; high prices later cut oil intensity and drew new non-OPEC supply.

rhymes.title: Volcker's Fed tightens sharply during the second oil shock
rhymes.rhyme: A Fed raising rates into an oil shock, as markets now price for Dec 9.

rhymes.title: Black Monday: the Dow falls 22.6% in a day
rhymes.rhyme: A crash after long-term yields had risen sharply through the year; today's 10-year is near 5%.

rhymes.title: Operation Praying Mantis: US-Iran naval battle in the Gulf
rhymes.rhyme: The Tanker War (1984-88) saw US escorts, tanker strikes and direct US-Iran clashes before a ceasefire that August.

rhymes.title: Iraq invades Kuwait; oil spikes; US recession under way (Jul 1990 - Mar 1991)
rhymes.rhyme: A Gulf war oil shock coinciding with a US recession.

rhymes.title: Fed hikes into an energy shock; two negative GDP quarters; Nasdaq bear market
rhymes.rhyme: The closest data analogue to now (see the analogue table): rising yields, an energy shock, and a Nasdaq drawdown of more than 30%.
